units.source: Vim mode
units.context: Vim mode

units.source: New to Vim? Start with the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Vim beginner guide__TRILIUM_PH_1__, which explains what the modes are and which keys to learn first.
units.context: Vim mode

units.source: Vim mode brings Vim-style modal editing to text notes: the motions, operators and commands of the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Vim__TRILIUM_PH_1__ text editor, in Trilium's own editor. It understands the structure of rich text: a paragraph, a heading, a list item or a table cell is a line, and so is an image or an included note.
units.context: Vim mode

units.source: The most used keys are in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Cheat sheet__TRILIUM_PH_1__ below, and all of them in the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Vim full reference__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
units.context: Vim mode

units.source: Enabling Vim mode__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Vim mode > Enabling Vim mode

units.source: Go to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Text Notes__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__Features__TRILIUM_PH_5__.
units.context: Vim mode > Enabling Vim mode

units.source: Turn on __TRILIUM_PH_0__Vim mode__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
units.context: Vim mode > Enabling Vim mode

units.source: The option applies to the current device only, so repeat these steps on each device where you want Vim mode. It takes effect at once, without a reload. Code notes have an option of their own: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Code Notes__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__Editor__TRILIUM_PH_5__ → __TRILIUM_PH_6__Vim keybindings__TRILIUM_PH_7__.
units.context: Vim mode > Enabling Vim mode

units.source: Once Vim mode is on:
units.context: Vim mode > Enabling Vim mode

units.source: Newly opened text notes start in Normal mode: press __TRILIUM_PH_0__ to type, and __TRILIUM_PH_1__Esc__TRILIUM_PH_2__ to return to the commands.
units.context: Vim mode > Enabling Vim mode

units.source: The notes that were already open when Vim mode was turned on switch to Insert mode, so you can continue typing.
units.context: Vim mode > Enabling Vim mode

units.source: In Insert mode, the regular editor stays available, with its formatting, slash commands, Markdown-like formatting and toolbars. A few shortcuts follow Vim there too, see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Shortcuts that change in the editor__TRILIUM_PH_1__ below.
units.context: Vim mode > Enabling Vim mode

units.source: Where Vim mode shows__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Vim mode > Enabling Vim mode > Where Vim mode shows

units.source: Vim mode uses three places of the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Status bar__TRILIUM_PH_1__, at the bottom of the window:
units.context: Vim mode > Enabling Vim mode > Where Vim mode shows

units.source: The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Vim__TRILIUM_PH_1__ badge, before the other indicators of the status bar, is highlighted while Vim mode is on for the current note. Click it to turn Vim mode off or on for that note, see __TRILIUM_PH_2__Vim mode for a single note__TRILIUM_PH_3__ below. Right-click it for a menu with the same switch, a switch for the key hints, the settings and this page.
units.context: Vim mode > Enabling Vim mode > Where Vim mode shows

units.source: The __TRILIUM_PH_0__mode indicator__TRILIUM_PH_1__, after the badge, shows the current mode: __TRILIUM_PH_2__, __TRILIUM_PH_3__, __TRILIUM_PH_4__, __TRILIUM_PH_5__ or __TRILIUM_PH_6__. Beside it appear the keys of a command that is not complete yet, short messages and the macro being recorded.
units.context: Vim mode > Enabling Vim mode > Where Vim mode shows

units.source: The area of the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Breadcrumb__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is used for two things: the key hints, described below, and the command line, which opens there when you press __TRILIUM_PH_2__, __TRILIUM_PH_3__ or __TRILIUM_PH_4__.
units.context: Vim mode > Enabling Vim mode > Where Vim mode shows

units.source: In __TRILIUM_PH_0__Zen mode__TRILIUM_PH_1__, the key hints, the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Vim__TRILIUM_PH_3__ badge and the mode indicator are visible.
units.context: Vim mode > Enabling Vim mode > Where Vim mode shows

units.source: Startup commands__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Vim mode > Settings > Startup commands

units.source: Write one command per line, as it would be typed after __TRILIUM_PH_0__. A line that starts with __TRILIUM_PH_1__ is a comment.
units.context: Vim mode > Settings > Startup commands

units.source: When you edit the list, the commands run again as soon as you leave the field, and their mappings replace those of the previous list. Changing the other settings does not run them again. Only the commands of Vim mode are understood, so a __TRILIUM_PH_0__ file made for Vim does not work as it is.
units.context: Vim mode > Settings > Startup commands

units.source: Vim mode for a single note__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Vim mode > Settings > Vim mode for a single note

units.source: To decide for one note, whatever the option says, add a __TRILIUM_PH_0__label__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to it:
units.context: Vim mode > Settings > Vim mode for a single note

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__ turns Vim mode on in that note.
units.context: Vim mode > Settings > Vim mode for a single note

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__ keeps that note in the regular editor.
units.context: Vim mode > Settings > Vim mode for a single note

units.source: The label can be inherited, so one label can cover a whole subtree. A label set on the note itself wins over an inherited one: with an inheritable __TRILIUM_PH_0__ on a parent note, a child note that has __TRILIUM_PH_1__ stays in the regular editor.
units.context: Vim mode > Settings > Vim mode for a single note

units.source: While the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Vim mode__TRILIUM_PH_1__ option is on, the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Vim__TRILIUM_PH_3__ badge in the status bar sets this label for you: a click on it gives the current note __TRILIUM_PH_4__, and another click removes that label again, or sets __TRILIUM_PH_5__ where the note would inherit __TRILIUM_PH_6__. When the label of the note is inheritable, the click changes Vim mode for the notes under it too, and its menu says so.
units.context: Vim mode > Settings > Vim mode for a single note

units.source: Key hints__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Vim mode > Key hints

units.source: Key hints help while you learn, and can be turned off once the keys are familiar. They show in the status bar, in the area of the breadcrumb:
units.context: Vim mode > Key hints

units.source: In Normal and Visual mode, the most used keys of the mode take the place of the breadcrumb. To switch between the keys and the breadcrumb, press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Esc__TRILIUM_PH_1__ in Normal mode. This is the last thing __TRILIUM_PH_2__Esc__TRILIUM_PH_3__ does: when something else applies, such as search highlights to clear, that happens first and it takes another press. See __TRILIUM_PH_4__The Esc key__TRILIUM_PH_5__ below.
units.context: Vim mode > Key hints

units.source: After a pause in the middle of a command, such as after __TRILIUM_PH_0__ or __TRILIUM_PH_1__, the keys that can follow are shown.
units.context: Vim mode > Key hints

units.source: The command line suggests the commands that match what is typed, and __TRILIUM_PH_0__Tab__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or the arrow keys complete them. The search prompt tells how the pattern is read.
units.context: Vim mode > Key hints

units.source: To see every key of the current mode, click the mode indicator or press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Alt__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__F1__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
units.context: Vim mode > Key hints

units.source: To turn the hints off, use the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Key hints__TRILIUM_PH_1__ setting or type __TRILIUM_PH_2__. __TRILIUM_PH_3__ turns them back on.
units.context: Vim mode > Key hints

units.source: How Vim reads a text note__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Vim mode > How Vim reads a text note

units.source: Vim works with lines, and a text note has none of its own. This is how the two fit together:
units.context: Vim mode > How Vim reads a text note

units.source: Each paragraph, heading, paragraph of a list item, paragraph of a table cell and line of a code block is one line, however many lines it takes on the screen. This is sometimes called a __TRILIUM_PH_0__logical line__TRILIUM_PH_1__, as opposed to a __TRILIUM_PH_2__screen line__TRILIUM_PH_3__. __TRILIUM_PH_4__, __TRILIUM_PH_5__, __TRILIUM_PH_6__ and __TRILIUM_PH_7__ act on logical lines, while __TRILIUM_PH_8__ and __TRILIUM_PH_9__ move by screen line.
units.context: Vim mode > How Vim reads a text note

units.source: An image, a diagram, a horizontal rule or an included note is also one line: __TRILIUM_PH_0__ and __TRILIUM_PH_1__ stop on it and __TRILIUM_PH_2__ deletes it. __TRILIUM_PH_3__ or __TRILIUM_PH_4__ enters its caption or its content. To leave an included note, press __TRILIUM_PH_5__Esc__TRILIUM_PH_6__ in its Normal mode, __TRILIUM_PH_7__ on its first line or __TRILIUM_PH_8__ on its last line.
units.context: Vim mode > How Vim reads a text note

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__ and __TRILIUM_PH_1__ add what __TRILIUM_PH_2__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_3__ would add at that place, such as a paragraph, a list item or a code line. __TRILIUM_PH_4__ joins lines the way __TRILIUM_PH_5__Backspace__TRILIUM_PH_6__ does. __TRILIUM_PH_7__ and __TRILIUM_PH_8__ change the level of a list item or the indentation of a paragraph.
units.context: Vim mode > How Vim reads a text note

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__, __TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__ and __TRILIUM_PH_3__ work with blocks instead of blank lines: a paragraph, a list item, a quote, a table cell, a code block. On a heading, __TRILIUM_PH_4__ is the heading together with its section.
units.context: Vim mode > How Vim reads a text note

units.source: In a table, __TRILIUM_PH_0__ and __TRILIUM_PH_1__ stay inside the cell, and __TRILIUM_PH_2__ and __TRILIUM_PH_3__ move down and up the column.
units.context: Vim mode > How Vim reads a text note

units.source: A collapsed heading or list item counts as one line for __TRILIUM_PH_0__ and __TRILIUM_PH_1__. Searching also looks inside it, and expands the one that holds a match.
units.context: Vim mode > How Vim reads a text note

units.source: Registers are shared by all text notes, but not with code notes. To carry text between the two, use the clipboard register __TRILIUM_PH_0__.
units.context: Vim mode > How Vim reads a text note

units.context: Vim mode > Shortcuts that change in the editor

units.source: Vim uses some of the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__ shortcuts of Trilium. While the cursor is in a text note, Vim's meaning wins, as it already does in code notes. units.source: The Esc key__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Vim mode > Shortcuts that change in the editor > The Esc key

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Esc__TRILIUM_PH_1__ does one thing per press, the first of these that applies:
units.context: Vim mode > Shortcuts that change in the editor > The Esc key

units.source: Closes what is open: the command line or the search prompt, a popup such as the link balloon, a completion list or the list of keys.
units.context: Vim mode > Shortcuts that change in the editor > The Esc key

units.source: Cancels the keys typed so far of a command.
units.context: Vim mode > Shortcuts that change in the editor > The Esc key

units.source: Leaves Visual or Insert mode.
units.context: Vim mode > Shortcuts that change in the editor > The Esc key

units.source: Clears the search highlights.
units.context: Vim mode > Shortcuts that change in the editor > The Esc key

units.source: In an included note, returns to the note around it.
units.context: Vim mode > Shortcuts that change in the editor > The Esc key

units.source: Switches between the key hints and the breadcrumb, when the key hints are on.
units.context: Vim mode > Shortcuts that change in the editor > The Esc key

units.source: So with a link balloon open in Insert mode, the first press closes the balloon and the second one leaves Insert mode. __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__[__TRILIUM_PH_3__ does the same as __TRILIUM_PH_4__Esc__TRILIUM_PH_5__.
units.context: Vim mode > Shortcuts that change in the editor > The Esc key

units.source: Limitations__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Vim mode > Limitations

units.source: Vim mode imitates Vim, it does not run Vim itself. Plugins and scripts made for Vim are not available, and some of its commands are missing: see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Not supported__TRILIUM_PH_1__ in the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Vim full reference__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
units.context: Vim mode > Limitations

units.source: Vim mode is not available in the mobile layout, and read-only notes have no modes.
units.context: Vim mode > Limitations

units.source: Visual Block mode is not supported. __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__V__TRILIUM_PH_3__ pastes, except in Insert mode when __TRILIUM_PH_4__Vim keys in Insert mode__TRILIUM_PH_5__ is on.
units.context: Vim mode > Limitations

units.source: Search patterns are JavaScript regular expressions, not Vim's own, and a match cannot span more than one line.
units.context: Vim mode > Limitations

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__ and __TRILIUM_PH_1__ only show a message: notes are saved as you type, so there is nothing to discard.
units.context: Vim mode > Limitations
